question: In thread cutting operations, symbols 1 and 2 indicate _____ and _____. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51171c70f9de8daaee558c971e31de61809b5ed7054a06b0391853f37bb51dc4.png]
solution:
**Concept**

 
• In engineering drawings and machining operations, specific symbols are used to denote the movement and engagement of the cutting tool.
 
• During thread cutting on a lathe, the process involves two critical phases: engaging the tool into the workpiece and retracting it at the end of the thread.
 
• The symbol for starting a cut usually indicates the tool moving toward or into the material, while the symbol for pulling off indicates the tool moving away from the material.

**Explanation**

In the context of thread cutting operations represented by standardized symbols:

 
• **Symbol 1:** This symbol typically indicates the **Start Cut**. it represents the point where the cutting tool makes contact with the workpiece and begins the threading process.
 
• **Symbol 2:** This symbol typically indicates the **Pull Off** (or Retraction). It represents the point where the tool is withdrawn from the groove or the workpiece surface at the end of the threading pass to prevent damage to the threads and to return to the starting position.

Therefore, in a sequence of operations for thread cutting, the tool must first start the cut and subsequently pull off after the required length is achieved.

**Hence, symbols 1 and 2 indicate Start Cut and Pull Off respectively.**</p
